From Wiktionary, the free dictionary

English

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From mute +‎ -er.

Adjective

[edit]

muter

  1. comparative form of mute: more mute

Noun

[edit]

muter (plural muters)

  1. Something that mutes sound.
    The violinist often uses a muter when she practices.

Related terms

[edit]
  • mute

Anagrams

[edit]
  • turme

French

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from Latin mūtāre. Doublet of muer.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /my.te/
  • Audio (France (Lyon)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Somain)):(file)

Verb

[edit]

muter

  1. to transfer
  2. to mutate

Romani

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Sanskrit मूत्र (mū́tra).[1][2][3] Compare Palula múutr.[2]

Noun

[edit]

muter m (nominative plural mutera or mutra)

  1. urine[2][3]

Derived terms

[edit]
  • mutrel
